content.title: Components Have Boundaries
content.hook: A React application can technically put an entire screen into one component.
content.context:
That does not make it a good design. Imagine this: ```jsx function Dashboard() { return (
Forge Admin

Orders

Order #1042
Order #1043
Account summary
); } ``` Nothing is illegal here. The question is whether the component has become responsible for too many meaningful pieces at once. A component boundary is useful when it gives a piece of UI a **name, responsibility, reuse point, or change boundary**.
goals: Decide what deserves to become a React component and explain why a boundary improves reasoning, reuse, or changeability.

content.question: Which is the strongest reason to extract the repeated order row into its own component?

options.text: Every HTML element must have a React component.
A repeated, meaningful UI piece now has one definition that can be reused and changed in one place.
React refuses to render repeated markup unless it is a component.

feedback.correct: Component boundaries are about reasoning and responsibility. File size alone is not a sufficient design rule.
feedback.incorrect: Component boundaries are about reasoning and responsibility. File size alone is not a sufficient design rule.

content.title: Name the responsibility
Build the boundary
What changed?
content.text:
The screen should still look the same.

That is important.

Good refactoring often changes the **structure of the code** while preserving the **behavior of the product**.

options.text: Yes. Every element deserves a component.
No. A component boundary should solve a meaningful problem, not satisfy a quota.

feedback.correct: A wrapper with no useful responsibility can add indirection without improving the design.
feedback.incorrect: A wrapper with no useful responsibility can add indirection without improving the design.

content.title: Boundary test
content.text:
Before extracting a component, ask:

**What would become easier because this has a name?**

Possible good answers include:

- I can reuse this piece.
- I can reason about this piece separately.
- It changes for a different reason than its parent.
- Its API can stay stable while its internals change.

options.text: `DashboardLine27` because the code on line 27 is getting long.
`OrderRow` because the UI represents a repeated concept with a clear responsibility.

feedback.correct: Good component names describe product concepts or responsibilities, not editor coordinates.
feedback.incorrect: Good component names describe product concepts or responsibilities, not editor coordinates.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A component boundary is an engineering boundary, not merely a visual box.
**Senior habit:** Extract a component because it makes the system easier to reason about or change—not because the file feels long.
